sections.hypothesis: Buying an altcoin at the close after it has fallen more than 30% over 7 days, and holding it for 3 days, beats holding the same coin on Sharpe after costs, on most coins it was never searched on.
sections.rationale: Who pays: in a crash, forced and panicked sellers (liquidated leverage, stop-losses, capitulation) push a small coin below what patient buyers will pay, and whoever provides liquidity at the bottom is paid when it bounces. Outside evidence is thin for crypto; short-term reversal is documented in equities (Jegadeesh 1990, Lehmann 1990). Against it, honestly: this is the reversal family, which Kestrel's rules name as rejected (its BTC and ETH dip tests failed); here it is only extreme falls in small coins. Where it came from: the exploration half (research/exploration/log.md): beat holding on 67% of the 181 exploration coins (41% in both halves) and on 29 of a 40-coin engine sample, in the market about 6% of the time. Profits came from many separate crashes (2020-03, 2021-04, 2022-05, 2022-11, 2024-04, 2024-08, 2025-02, 2025-10), the best two months 26%, but concentrated in a few trades per coin. None of that is evidence.
sections.rules: crash-rebound with its defaults, one coin at a time, daily bars, spot, long only: at a close where the coin is more than 30% below its close 7 days earlier, fully into the coin for 3 days (that close and the next two; a new crash extends it), else cash. Decide at the close, trade at the next open; 2% no-trade band. Every confirmation-half coin with 24+ months before 2025-11-01, from its first bar.
sections.falsification: Pre-registered (CLAUDE.md, Exploration experiment), run once with kestrel confirm on every confirmation-half coin with 24+ months of daily bars before 2025-11-01: PASS only if (1) the strategy's Sharpe after costs beats holding the same coin on more than half of those coins, and (2) across every coin's walk-forward test windows pooled (24-month training, 6-month tests, the fixed rule), it beats holding's Sharpe in more than half; a coin too short for one 24 + 6-month window adds no windows but still counts for (1). Otherwise FAIL. The method itself works if at least one of the two graduates passes. A pass is not a pursue: the graduate would still need its own scorecard and holdout note.
sections.parameters: drop_pct 30, days 7, hold_days 3: chosen in exploration, fixed here. No other setting is run on the confirmation half.
sections.costs: Daily bars, 330 USDT; costs from kestrel.toml: 7.5 bps fee a side and each coin's spread band from its 30-day median daily volume (8-15 bps a side for most altcoins). One look in the confirmation trial pool; nothing here counts in the main luck bar. Few trades (a handful of crashes a year a coin), each paying a full round trip at a crashed coin's wide spread.
